passages.provision_quote: “Race” is inclusive of traits historically associated with race, including, but not limited to, hair texture and protective hairstyles.
passages.note: Bill text page; amends Education Code and FEHA race definition to close a discrimination-enforcement gap for hairstyles.
Senate floor vote page; Caballero voted Aye, 37-0-1.

rows.reasoning: Caballero voted Aye (37-0-1) on SB 188, which amends the Education Code and Government Code definitions of race to include hair texture and protective hairstyles, closing an enforcement gap for race-based grooming discrimination. This matches the rung text "strengthen civil rights enforcement and address systemic discrimination," since the bill expands what antidiscrimination law covers and its findings name a documented systemic effect; it does not mandate equity requirements across all institutions nor merely maintain existing law.
